name: Chisel
text: Legal publishes a *time-stamped, auto-approved queue* for repurposed assets, with Product Ops responsible for logging every auto-cleared item. Legal retains the right to audit the queue weekly and retroactively block anything that violates the red-line playbook. This shifts the bottleneck from real-time approval to targeted review, cutting repurposing delays while keeping Legal’s oversight intact. The trade-off: some risky assets may slip through before Legal catches them, but the weekly audit limits exposure and forces Product Ops to justify their decisions.

name: Sift
text: The real risk isn’t edge cases slipping—it’s Product Ops gaming the system by over-escalating trivial issues to avoid accountability. Instead, Legal should publish the playbook but require Product Ops to batch and timestamp edge cases weekly, with Legal reviewing only the batch, not individual requests. This forces discipline without creating a new bottleneck.

name: Scope
text: Legal publishes a single, public "Repurpose Rules Matrix"—a one-page table listing every repurposing rule with a clear yes/no/ask-Legal column. Product Ops runs the queue: if the rule says yes, auto-clear; if no, auto-block; if ask-Legal, escalate with a timestamped log. This cuts Legal’s workload to only the 10% of cases where the matrix forces their hand, while keeping repurposing fast and transparent. Trade-off: the matrix must stay ruthlessly simple—no edge-case exceptions, or Product Ops will exploit gaps to shift blame.

name: Scriv
text: The real risk isn’t Product Ops gaming the system—it’s Legal gaming the system by hiding behind the playbook to avoid making hard calls. Instead, Legal should publish the playbook but *require* Product Ops to flag only the top 5% most ambiguous cases for Legal review—no more, no less. That settles it: clear threshold, measurable load, and Legal can’t duck accountability.
